races.title: State House, District 63
races.note: Unopposed: this seat was decided without a general-election contest, so it won't be on your ballot.

cands.name: Jacqueline Coffie-Leeks
cands.bio: Executive director of the Sulphur Springs Neighborhood of Promise Initiative. Her campaign says she has worked with Hillsborough residents for 45+ years and spent 12 years on a statewide initiative that secured and managed $30 million+ in state funding. Democrat; unopposed in November.
cands.local_ties: Works in the Sulphur Springs neighborhood of Tampa (Florida Politics, Axios); her campaign site cites 45+ years working directly with Hillsborough County residents.

record.text: Executive director, Sulphur Springs Neighborhood of Promise Initiative (named in a Florida Politics fundraising report). Has not held a legislative office. The name 'Jacqueline Leeks' on Ballotpedia is tied to a 2016 Hillsborough School Board ballot per a search listing; identity not independently confirmed.

money_notes.text: Through June 26 she had raised about $25,000. Reported donors in the latest period included $1,000 from Voice of Florida Business PAC (linked to Associated Industries of Florida), plus pastor Clethen Sutton and YMCA CEO Matt Mitchell.

endorsements.text: Florida Realtors PAC endorsed her in HD 63.
Florida Chamber of Commerce included her in its second wave of 2026 legislative endorsements (listed as 'Coffee-Leeks').

cands.gaps: No Tampa Bay Times endorsement found. No campaign-finance totals after June 26 found. No controversies found. Owner-source search (Stew Peters / Alex Jones / Owen Shroyer) was NOT run: the shared web-search budget was exhausted, so no owner-source status is known.
